$comment: The source lock of 105's migration packet: what was checked against upstream, how, and when, resolved afresh on 2026-11-14 rather than taken from the historical README. Revisions are named as in target.json. 'files' gives the git blob id (git hash-object) of each source file the selected method depends on, at each revision. 'correspondence' records the published artifacts that carry the same sources, and how their class was compared. Checked by hand by the positive stream; a note, not evidence of a build or a replay.
how: git init --bare; git fetch --filter=blob:none https://github.com/apache/commons-numbers.git refs/heads/master refs/pull/223/head refs/tags/rel/commons-numbers-1.3 (the branch and the pull request's ref only to find the commits, which are then pinned by SHA); parents read from the commit objects; blob ids with git rev-parse REV:PATH; Maven Central JARs fetched with curl and their sha1 compared with Central's .sha1 files; the sources JAR's file hashed with git hash-object

historicalReport.$comment: What README.md (2026-11-01) names, checked against the above: 'merged 2026-10-18 as 8cfc04e8' is after; 'the head commit 79aa4643' is pr-head; 'e7c172d2 (the commit the squash merge landed on, whose copy of the file is the pre-fix one)' is before. pr-head and after carry the same ArithmeticUtils.java, so the report's classes and this packet's come from the same two source files. The report's verdicts are not re-derived here.

dependencies.$comment: pow(int,int) calls Math.multiplyExact(int,int) and the constructors of IllegalArgumentException (with a StringBuilder message), ArithmeticException and Object; nothing outside java.base. ArithmeticUtils has no static initializer: its two String fields are compile-time constants. Its nested class NumbersArithmeticException is not reached by pow(int,int). The Maven build's own dependency closure (commons-parent 105, org.apache:apache:39, the plugins it binds, commons-rng at test scope) is runtime's preparation record, not this lock's.

correspondence.bytecode: before's ArithmeticUtils.java compiled alone with JDK 11.0.33's javac --release 8 gives a class (sha256 550e4dca…) that differs from the published one in bytes but not in javap -c -p -constants output once constant-pool indices are masked: the same bytecode, laid out differently. after's file compiled the same way (5f0c0d8d…) differs from before's in two instructions only, if_icmplt to if_icmple in pow(int,int) and pow(long,int).
